cover.title: Freakonomics
cover.author: Steven D. Levitt & Stephen J. Dubner

segments.text: A father named his two sons Winner and Loser. One became a decorated NYPD detective. The other ended up in handcuffs. Guess which.
You guessed wrong. LOSER Lane became the detective. Winner became the criminal. The name scripted neither life.
The data says a name barely moves a child's future. What moves it is who the parents already are.
The name just marks the parents; it doesn't cause the outcome. It's the classic trap: correlation isn't causation.
